fields.title: Microsoft's Azure growth falls below 48% in its January 27 report
fields.text: At its fiscal second-quarter report, projected for January 27, 2027, Microsoft reports constant-currency growth in Azure and other cloud services below 48% for the December quarter: the acceleration from 48% in the September quarter stalls or reverses.

chances.note: Azure beat its own guidance by three to four points last quarter (48% against 44%-45%), and analysts look for 49%-50%. A print under 48% needs that pattern to break. What could break it: capacity ('capacity constraints prevented Azure from growing even faster'), this month's outages, and capital spending that already came in below expectations. I put it a little above one in five.

passages: Slowinski highlighted 48% constant-currency Azure growth in the fiscal first quarter, above management’s 44%-45% guidance, while Microsoft 365 Commercial Cloud grew 18%.
He expects Azure growth to accelerate further to 49%-50% in the fiscal second quarter and Microsoft 365 Commercial Cloud growth to reach 19%.
Munster also said capacity constraints prevented Azure from growing even faster, reinforcing Microsoft’s need for additional infrastructure investment.

to.title: Azure grows 48% to 50%, about as expected
to.text: Microsoft reports constant-currency Azure growth from 48.0% up to and including 50.0% for the December quarter at its January 27, 2027 report.

to.title: Azure growth accelerates above 50%
to.text: Microsoft reports constant-currency Azure growth above 50.0% for the December quarter at its January 27, 2027 report.

chances.note: Another beat of the size of last quarter's against a 49%-50% expectation puts growth above 50%. Microsoft has beaten its Azure guidance in recent quarters, but capacity is the limit management cites, so I put this a little above one in four.

shock.note: Microsoft has fallen from $554 on Nov 4 to $500 as outages and the software selloff hit it. A clear acceleration answers Dan Ives's 'six-month window' for AI to show monetisation; the shares rose about 6% on Nov 4 when investors rotated back to it. 5% beyond what the shares would otherwise do.

Azure's acceleration is the reason analysts hold targets of $610-$722 with free cash flow set to turn negative in the second half of the fiscal year on capital spending. A stall would put the spending without the growth; Alphabet lost 11.8% in a day on Oct 29 for a capex-heavy quarter with negative free cash flow. I use 7% beyond what Microsoft would otherwise do.
